claim: Ubuntu LTS gets 5 years standard security maintenance, 10 years with Ubuntu Pro ESM, 15 years with the Legacy add-on; interim releases get 9 months.
quote: LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance. ... ESM extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the 'Main' repository ... the Legacy add-on can be purchased to cover additional 5 years of the lifetime of Ubuntu LTS, giving a total of 15 years

claim: Debian 13 trixie gets 3 years of full support to 9 Aug 2028 plus 2 years of LTS to 30 Jun 2030.
quote: the initial three years of full Debian support until August 9th, 2028, and two years of Long Term Support (LTS) until June 30th, 2030

claim: Each Fedora release is supported until 4 weeks after release X+2, i.e. roughly 13 months; Fedora 44 (Apr 2026) ends 2 Jun 2027.
quote: Release X is supported until 4 weeks after the release of Release X+2 and with approximately 6 months between most versions, meaning a version of Fedora is usually supported for at least 13 months, possibly longer.

claim: Every openSUSE Leap 16 minor release receives 24 months of community maintenance, double the Leap 15 series.
quote: Leap 16 will take things even further by supporting users with maintenance updates over two releases, giving each release a full 24 months of community support.

claim: openSUSE Leap 15.6 reached EOL at the end of April 2026 and moving to Leap 16 requires a dedicated migration tool.
quote: Leap 15.6 will reach End of Life (EOL) at the close of this month. ... You can download openSUSE Leap 16 and use the migration tool to upgrade

claim: Rocky Linux 10 has general support to 31 May 2030 and security support to 31 May 2035 — a 10-year lifecycle matching RHEL.
quote: Rocky 10 (Code Name "Red Quartz") has general support until 31 May 2030 and security support through 31 May 2035

claim: Arch publishes breaking-change and manual-intervention notices that must be read before upgrading; only 4 news items appeared in the first seven months of 2026.
quote: 2026-07-21 virtualbox-ext-vnc >= 7.2.12-2 requires manual intervention; 2026-06-12 Active AUR malicious packages incident; 2026-06-04 Arch Linux 2026 Leader Election Results; 2026-05-25 Breaking changes for all users of varnish

claim: The December 2025 .NET 9 to 10 transition on Arch required users to intervene manually during the upgrade.
Third-party PPAs are the most common cause of do-release-upgrade failures; the upgrader disables them, leaving their packages in a broken state.
quote: Third-party PPAs are the single most common cause of upgrade failures, with packages built for 24.04 conflicting with the 26.04 repository during dependency resolution.

claim: Fedora's automatic updates use the opt-in dnf-automatic package configured via /etc/dnf/automatic.conf, preset to install security-classified updates.
quote: The service is configured via the /etc/dnf/automatic.conf, which has been pre-configured to automatically install packages classified as 'security' updates.

claim: Atomic Fedora derivatives stage each update as a new deployment, always keep a rollback deployment, and move major version via rpm-ostree rebase.
quote: You always have two deployments at minimum: the one you're running and the one you'll roll back to. Each rpm-ostree operation stages a new deployment. Nothing changes until you reboot.

claim: Linux Mint 22.x is supported until April 2029 and Mint 23 is targeted for December 2026.
quote: Linux Mint 22.x is supported until April 2029. ... The team has confirmed December 2026 as its target

claim: The ArchWiki is treated as the authoritative Linux configuration reference by users of other distributions, while Ubuntu's help is higher-volume but more variable in quality.
quote: many Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian users consult it regularly for topics where their own distribution's documentation is thin or outdated
